answers_by_date.answer: Only major convictions (e.g., criminal offenses) can lead to loss of citizenship status
answers_by_date.basis: In force: Constitution 1980 art. 11 nº3 (loss of nationality 'por sentencia judicial condenatoria por delitos contra la dignidad de la patria o los intereses esenciales y permanentes del Estado') and nº4 (cancellation of the carta), plus DS 5142/1960 art. 8 (cancellation for conviction under State Security Law 12.927 or 'ocurrencias que hagan indigno'). Only serious/state-security offences reach nationality. No documented cancellation practice found for this period.

answers_by_date.answer: Only major convictions (e.g., criminal offenses) can lead to loss of citizenship status
answers_by_date.basis: Same text as 2000: Ley 20.050, which repealed art. 11 nº3, was published and in force only on 26-08-2005, after this date. DS 5142 art. 8 unchanged. No practice evidence of cancellations found.

answers_by_date.answer: Only major convictions (e.g., criminal offenses) can lead to loss of citizenship status
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 20.050 (26-08-2005) repealed the constitutional conviction ground; loss now only via cancellation of the carta, which DS 5142 art. 8 still allows for State Security Law convictions or 'indignidad'. Same option, narrower grounds. No documented cancellations found.

answers_by_date.answer: Only major convictions (e.g., criminal offenses) can lead to loss of citizenship status
answers_by_date.basis: Constitution art. 11 (post-2005) and DS 5142 art. 8 unchanged; Ley 20.888 (2016) did not touch art. 8. No practice evidence of cancellations for convictions found; government releases 2011-2013 report only grants.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 but they are not the same

answers.sourcing_note: DS 5142 art. 8 read in the 1960 and 2016 LeyChile versions (identical) and in the current text. The pre-2005 Constitution art. 11 was read from a reproduction (diputados.gob.mx) and the Ley 20.050 amending text on LeyChile. No documented cancellation of a carta for a conviction was found for any period, so implementation rests on absence of evidence.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The MRD's 2020 implementation 'Rarely; Effectively Always' pairs non-neighbouring levels and is not an allowed option; I rated past dates 'Usually; Effectively Always' because no cancellation is documented. Ley 21.325 arts. 86/88, cited by the MRD, were not in force in 2020; the 2020 answer rests on DS 5142 art. 8 and Constitution art. 11.
answers.notes: Arts. 16-17 of the Constitution concern ciudadanía (voting/political rights), not nationality; Ley 20.050 amended them but they do not affect nationality status. The 'indignidad' ground in DS 5142 art. 8 is open-ended, but the explicit conviction ground is limited to State Security Law offences. A 2026 inaplicabilidad filing against art. 8 DL 747 was seen only in search results (not read) and is outside the period.

answers_by_date.basis: Constitution art. 10 nº4 (carta de nacionalización, with renunciation of prior nationality unless a treaty applies) and DS 5142 art. 2 (21 years, more than five years' continuous residence, permanencia definitiva per DL 1432/1976). Economic migrants reached permanencia definitiva via DL 1094 arts. 23 (sujeto a contrato, after two years) and 31 (temporario). Practice evidence thin: the Interior 2013 release covers naturalisations over the prior ten years (from about 2003).

Same text as 2000 (Ley 20.050 entered into force 26-08-2005). Practice: the Interior 2013 release reports naturalisations of people from over 112 countries over the preceding decade; no specific data read for 2005.

Ley 20.050 (2005) replaced art. 10 nº4 with 'Los extranjeros que obtuvieren carta de nacionalización en conformidad a la ley', dropping the constitutional renunciation requirement. DS 5142 art. 2 unchanged. Practice: 1,189 people completed naturalisation between 2010 and Nov 2011 (Interior 2011).

Same law as 2010 (Ley 20.888, which lowered the age to 18, came into force 08-01-2016, after this date). Practice: applications rose 14% 2008-2012; 11,246 people naturalised 2010-2019 (Interior 2013; CNN Chile 2019).

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 but they are not the same

answers.starting_answer_concern: The 2020 implementation 'Rarely; Usually' pairs non-neighbouring levels and is not an allowed option; past dates rated 'Usually'. The MRD citation's 'pena aflictiva' bar and five-year term come from Ley 21.325; in 2020 the bars were DS 5142 art. 3 (any conviction or pending prosecution for crimes or simple delitos), and the minimum age was 18 only from 2016 (21 before).
answers.notes: DS 5142 art. 3 (pre-2022) barred applicants who had been convicted of, or were being prosecuted for, crimes or simple delitos; Ley 21.325 art. 175 nº11 deleted it (in force 2022). The 2018 regularisation and the 2018 visas changed residence practice, not the naturalisation statute.

answers_by_date.basis: Kept at the starting answer: no dated event between 2000 and 2020 changed refugees' access to naturalisation, so the past dates follow the 2020 'No'. But in force at this date: DL 1094 arts. 34-40 bis (asylum/refugee visa, Ley 19.476 of 1996), art. 37 (asylee may request permanencia definitiva after two years), and DS 5142 art. 2. No practice evidence specific to refugees.
Same law as 2000; kept at the starting answer (see concern). No refugee-specific practice evidence.
DL 1094 refugee provisions still in force (Ley 20.430, which gives refugees permanent residence, came into force 15-04-2010, after this date). Kept at the starting answer.

Ley 20.430 art. 45 (from 2010) entitles recognised refugees to permanent residence, which together with DS 5142 art. 2 is a route to naturalisation. Ley 20.507 (2011) added temporary residence for trafficking victims (DL 1094 art. 33 bis). Kept at the starting answer because no event explains a different coding; see concern.

answers.repealed_search: Searched DL 1094 (refugee/asylum provisions arts. 34-40 bis and permanencia definitiva arts. 41-42), Ley 20.430 (2010 original), DS 5142 versions (1960, 2016, 2022) and Ley 20.888. Found no humanitarian pathway that was repealed or narrowed before 2020. Instead, pathways were in force throughout: DL 1094 art. 37 until 2010, Ley 20.430 art. 45 from 2010, and DS 5142 art. 2, extended to refugees' children in 2016.

answers.sourcing_note: Ley 20.430 original text read via LeyChile JSON; DL 1094 read in its final consolidated text (refugee articles from Ley 19.476 of 1996, unchanged until 2010). No refugee-specific naturalisation statistics found.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The 2020 'No' looks wrong on its own date. Recognised refugees were entitled to permanent residence (Ley 20.430 art. 45) and, after more than five years' residence, could apply for a carta under DS 5142 art. 2. Ley 20.888 (2016) explicitly addressed refugees' children in DS 5142 art. 2. Before 2010, DL 1094 art. 37 let asylees obtain permanencia definitiva after two years. The statutory law supports 'Yes' on every date from 2000 to 2020; past dates were kept at 'No' only because no dated event explains a difference from the starting answer.
answers.notes: The MRD's 2023 answer ('Yes', citing Ley 21.325 art. 70) matches the statutory position that already existed before 2020. The 2019 CNN piece quotes the Interior undersecretary saying many naturalised people came from places with political persecution, which is weak practice evidence that humanitarian migrants did naturalise.

answers_by_date.basis: DS 5142 art. 2: the general route (five years' residence plus permanencia definitiva) and a pre-2016 final inciso letting children of naturalised parents obtain a carta at 18. Family migrants got temporario visas for family ties (DL 1094 art. 29) and permanencia definitiva after one year (art. 31). Constitution art. 10 nº3: children of Chileans born abroad became Chilean by living in Chile for more than one year. Practice for 2000 is thin.
Same as 2000 (Ley 20.050 in force only from 26-08-2005). Practice thin: the Interior 2013 release covers the prior decade.

Ley 20.050 replaced art. 10 nº3: children of Chileans born abroad are Chilean without the residence requirement, subject to a generational limit; the renunciation requirement was also removed. DS 5142 art. 2 and DL 1094 arts. 29/31 unchanged. Practice: 1,189 naturalisations 2010-2011, including families (Interior 2011).

Same law as 2010. Ley 20.888 (in force 08-01-2016) later let foreigners' children apply from 14, and refugees' children once a parent had naturalised. Practice: rising applications 2008-2012 (Interior 2013).

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 but they are not the same

Practice sources cover naturalisations generally, not family migrants specifically; nothing specific for 2000-2005.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The 2020 implementation 'Rarely; Usually' pairs non-neighbouring levels and is not an allowed option; past dates rated 'Usually'. The MRD's citation (Ley 21.325 art. 85: a reduced two-year term for spouses and relatives of Chileans) describes a provision that did not exist before 2022. In 2000-2020 there was no reduced term for spouses of Chileans; the family pathway was the general five-year route plus the provisions on children.
